text: Mulching and composting are two of the most effective gardening techniques for enhancing soil health and producing bountiful harvests. Mulching, the application of a layer of organic material such as straw, wood chips, or shredded leaves, serves to retain soil moisture, suppress weeds, and regulate soil temperature. By blocking sunlight, mulch also inhibits the growth of unwanted plants and encourages the growth of beneficial ones, as it adds nutrients back into the soil. Composting, the process of recycling organic waste into rich soil amendment, enriches the soil with essential nutrients and improves its structure and drainage. It reduces landfill waste, produces valuable fertilizer, and creates a natural soil conditioning process that enhances the vitality of any garden or plot. Both methods are sustainable and eco-friendly, contributing to a healthier planet through consistent, thoughtful gardening practices.
